profile.name: Joselito Villanueva Dizon
profile.statement: Making AI practical, personal, and meaningful in everyday life.
about: Experienced technology architect passionate about AI and innovation. I design and build AI systems end to end — from the model and the data to the API, the interface and the server it runs on.

MealSenseAI and CEREBRO were both developed as MVPs during my postgraduate studies in AI Systems at NUS — MealSenseAI applying machine learning, computer vision and conversational AI, CEREBRO knowledge representation and reasoning. Both projects here are self-hosted on my own home server and run their models locally.

projects.name: MealSenseAI
projects.tagline: Nutrition intelligence from a photo of your meal.
projects.description: Photograph a meal and MealSenseAI segments the plate, identifies each food and estimates its nutrition, showing how it reached every number. A Meal Advisor answers questions grounded in your own logged meals, and glucose-impact estimates in mmol/L are always labelled as estimates, never as measurements.
highlights: YOLO11 segmentation with an EfficientNet-B0 food classifier (Food-101 + FoodSG)
Explainable pipeline: every estimate shows its source and confidence
Grounded Meal Advisor on a local LLM via Ollama

subprojects.title: Data Engineering, Machine Learning and Model Evaluation
subprojects.summary: 310,861 images, a 320-class taxonomy and a leakage audit behind an EfficientNet-B0 classifier: 70.6% top-1 and 85.7% top-3 on 45,800 held-out images, with training and evaluation charts.

demo.summary: A five-minute narrated tour: why unlabelled meals are the gap in diabetes self-care, then one hawker lunch from photo to portions, glucose impact, a portion and walking what-if, and the Meal Advisor.
demo.note: Wei Ming and his meals are fictional. What you see is the real application and its real output. Educational estimates only, not medical advice.

projects.name: CEREBRO
projects.tagline: Adaptive Knowledge and Reasoning Digital Twin.
projects.description: CEREBRO turns personal documents and experience into a private, connected knowledge store — Learn, Connect, Reason, Recall. It ingests PDF, Word, PowerPoint and Markdown, proposes metadata for human approval, and answers questions with citations back to the exact fragment. A Galaxy view maps how topics connect; a Timeline orders what the documents themselves date.
highlights: Enrichment proposes, a person approves — provenance on every field
Hybrid keyword and semantic recall with local embeddings
Ask with citations, on a local model — no cloud AI engine

subprojects.title: Data Engineering, Machine Learning and Model Evaluation · Text documents
subprojects.summary: Search, topics and answering, tested on public benchmarks on my own GPU. Designed models search 3× better than the live setup (nDCG@10 0.73 vs 0.23).

subprojects.title: Data Engineering, Machine Learning and Model Evaluation · Images
subprojects.summary: Naming, describing and linking images, tested on 100 ImageNetV2 photos on my own GPU. ResNet-50 is right 71% of the time; the top similar image is relevant 65% of the time — good suggestions, still reviewed by a person.

demo.summary: A five-minute narrated tour: adding a document, search, the Knowledge Galaxy, the Timeline and Ask CEREBRO, on the documents of a fictional company.
demo.note: Larkspur Logistics and everything about it are invented. What you see is the real application and real output from local models.

projects.name: NEXUS
projects.tagline: Design in plain language. Find the bottleneck before it ships.
projects.description: Say what the system should do, then watch it take the load, find where it breaks and prove it is compliant, before anything is built. The architect designs in plain language; a local language model asks what it needs to know and returns an editable plan, and every step is dry-run before it is applied. A resiliency simulator pushes the design to 1,000× load, autoscales what can scale, prices it and names the component that breaks first. Every change is checked against the approved technology stack, enterprise architecture principles and cybersecurity policy, and recorded as a traceable, approved decision.
highlights: Natural-language design: conversation, clarifying questions, and plans the architect edits step by step
Resiliency simulation to 1,000× load: autoscaling, scale-in, monthly cost and a "safe up to" limit that names the bottleneck
Design governance by rule: every change checked against approved technology, EA principles, cybersecurity policy and MITRE ATT&CK
Traceability: versioned change ledger, architecture decision records and role-based approval, with the architect always in the loop
